subject: Procurement RFP + migration window for developer tooling (GitHub, JetBrains, Atlassian)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial seat counts + ask to start consolidated RFP

Team —

Attached is the current seat-count snapshot (sheet 'Oct-2026'). Procurement wants a single RFP that covers GitHub Enterprise, JetBrains floating seats, and Atlassian Cloud (jira + confluence). Goal: get vendor pricing and multi-year options so we can decide whether to consolidate or stagger renewals next Q.

Asks:
- Monica: can you own vendor outreach and timeline? I think we should aim to have RFP out by Oct 12.
- Karthik: please draft baseline SSO/SCIM + compliance requirements (SOC2, data residency, audit logs) — vendors will flag these early.
- Laura: liaise with Finance on preferred contract term (12 vs 36 months) and the approval path.

Constraints to keep in mind: our JetBrains renewal is Feb 2027 (floating), GitHub seat commit window is Mar 2027, Atlassian renews in Apr 2027. Looking for migration window options that minimize disruption (canary repo moves, phased Confluence space exports).

I attached the seat counts and a short RFP outline. If we want to include professional services (migration) estimates, note that several teams will need hands-on support (infra, mono-repo owners, docs).

Thanks — rishi

Attachments: 2026-10-05-devtools-seatcounts.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial seat counts + ask to start consolidated RFP

Rishi — good plan. I can run vendor outreach. Proposed timeline:
- Oct 8–9: finalize RFP doc internally
- Oct 12: send RFP to shortlisted vendors (GitHub, JetBrains, Atlassian + one reseller for JetBrains)
- Oct 20: vendor Q&A calls
- Nov 3: responses due; Nov 10: internal evaluation

I've attached a draft RFP (very rough) — it includes the baseline product asks, SSO/SCIM checklist, a stub for migration services, and evaluation criteria. I'm adding a vendor evaluation matrix sheet to the drive.

Notes:
- We should include a question for volume discount thresholds and true-up options for Cloud billing.
- Migration: ask for an estimated timeline and two pricing buckets: self-serve guidance vs. fully-managed services.

I'll set the Q&A calls and include procurement@acme-corp.com as a reference since they recently ran a consolidation and shared lessons learned.

— monica

Attachments: 2026-10-07-devtools-rfp-draft.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial seat counts + ask to start consolidated RFP

Updating with the SSO/SCIM and compliance checklist — pasted key asks below and added to the RFP doc.

Key technical requirements (summary):
- SAML 2.0 SSO + Okta/OneLogin templates; support for attribute mappings for teams and roles.
- SCIM provisioning for groups + members; delta updates < 60s preferred.
- Audit logs: tokenized export, retention >= 13 months, access via API and S3 export.
- Data residency: primary storage in us-west-2; replication ok in us-east-1.
- KV cache/CI pipeline hooks: need webhooks for repo events and Confluence space change events.

Also added a tiny section on migration rollback expectations (backout plans if a space import corrupts page structure). I flagged professional services as an optional line item and asked vendors to provide both fixed-price and T&M estimates.

I'll be on the vendor calls on Oct 20 to cover technical Qs.

— karthik
From: github-sales@github.com
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: GitHub Enterprise options + migration services — Q&A follow-up

Hi Monica and team —

Thanks for the RFP. Quick notes from the GitHub side after today's call:
- We can support SAML + SCIM with the provisioning cadence you requested; we recommend an incremental onboarding where you sync orgs by team to minimize risk.
- Pricing: attached a high-level quote for GitHub Enterprise Cloud and an optional premium migration services bundle for monorepo consolidation. Volume discounts kick in at 500+ seats; have included three term options (12/24/36 months).
- Audit logs: we provide 24 months of audit logs with API access; for S3 export we have a standard connector (estimate included).
- Can provide a two-week pilot for a subset of repos (5 teams) to validate CI triggers and the repo import tool.

Next steps: we'll upload the formal quote to the secure link and share a DocuSign for initial engagement. Please confirm whether you want the pilot scoped as PoC (no charge) or as a paid engagement.

Best,
Samira (GitHub Sales)

Attachments referenced: github-enterprise-quote-2026-10-20.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: github-sales@github.com, jetbrains-sales@jetbrains.com, atlasteam@atlassian.com
Date: 2026-10-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement RFP + migration window for developer tooling (GitHub, JetBrains, Atlassian)

Thanks all — good progress. Quick alignment notes and internal asks before we move to procurement sign-off:

Decisions to make this week:
1) Pilot approach: approve GitHub's two-week pilot (PoC) for 5 teams to validate CI and repo imports. Monica, please confirm scope and teams by EOD Oct 21.
2) Contract term: Laura, Finance prefers 24 months with an exit clause tied to headcount true-ups. Is that feasible from your side?
3) Migration phasing: propose 3 waves — Docs (Confluence) in Jan 2027, Repos (GitHub) Feb–Mar 2027 (parallel canary + staged pulls), JetBrains seat reassignment during Feb renewal window. Aim for full cutover by Apr 2027.

Procurement asks: once vendors upload quotes, procurement needs a single packet (vendor quotes, eval matrix, migration plan) to present at the Oct 28 purchasing review. Monica, can you assemble?

If procurement approves on Oct 28, we can trigger pilots and request DocuSign drafts for 24-month terms. Also want a clause for rollback support and a one-time migration warranty.

Thanks — rishi
